Late/Absence Procedures
It is really important that ALL absences from school need are reported to the school office by 9:30am at the latest on 01202 871577, via Classdojo, the school ParentMail app or to the school office email - office@oakhurstfirst.com.
If your child has been sick and/or has diarrhoea please inform the school office ASAP and keep your child at home for 48 hour after the last occurrence of either.
If you are running late please call the school office to let them know, if is safe to do so, on 01202 871577 and they will let the class teacher know and inform you which gate to enter the building through on your arrival.
Many thanks for your support with this.

Our curriculum
At Oakhurst First and Nursery School our curriculum is designed to inspire our children and encourage them to be inquisitive and develop awe and wonder so they have a love and thirst for learning.
We aim to ensure we have high ambitions and expectations for all of our children and provide them with a broad range of memorable experiences so they have strong dreams and ambitions about their future paths.
We encourage our children to develop reciprocal and collaborative skills so they build positive relationships, have strong sense of team and become respectful, valued members of the community.
Building resilience in a caring environment is threaded through our curriculum so children feel loved, safe, valued and have the confidence to be able to tackle and face challenges in a positive way.
Progression in all areas of the curriculum builds on what the children already know, encourages them to make links and develop the skills and knowledge they need in order to move onto the next stage of their education.
To find out more about our curriculum please contact Mrs Ann Clark

School Clubs
At Oakhurst we provide engaging before and after school clubs that further support our children and their families. Please see below for more information.
Breakfast Club - from 7.45am, everyday
Our breakfast club is run by school staff from 8am every morning. We offer a nutritious breakfast option and appropriate activities to start the school day and get the children ready for the day's learning ahead. Please see the below booking form for further information regarding pricing.
After School Club - 3pm-5.15pm Mon-Thurs, 3pm-4pm Fri
After School Club, is run by two members of school staff everyday.
The sessions include circle time so that the children can discuss their day and share the exciting activities they have taken part in during the day. They then have a nutritious snack, possibly sampling foods they haven't had before, which they can help to prepare. We have a range of themed activities that link through to what they might be learning in class currently to further support their learning. These might include cooking, experimenting, crafting, painting role play and reading.
Please see the below booking form regarding pricing.
Sports Club - TeamTheme Coaches - Football - Wednesdays and Dodgeball Thursdays 3-4pm
Three times a week after school we have a sports club that operates from 3-4pm that is run by TeamTheme coaches. Please speak to the school office for further details. In addition Team Theme come and run lunchtime sports clubs Tues, Wed and Thurs for any children from Years 1-4 who wishes to take part (no booking required)
If your child is in receipt of pupil premium funding, please speak to the school office about how we can support your child to access clubs.

English
At Oakhurst, we strive to develop a lifelong love of reading as well as reading for a purpose. We provide daily story and poetry time that excites and transports children into an imaginary world. The children are exposed to rich vocabulary and develop their story telling skills. Each story is carefully selected to provide a wide range of genres, contexts and language.
The children learn to read using a systematic phonics scheme called Read Write Inc as early as Nursery. Once fluent in decoding, they move onto the Read Write Inc Comprehension scheme where they deepen their understanding of a story by unpicking the plot, characters and settings. The children will make predictions, infer, sequence and retrieve information from a text. This continues in Key Stage 2 with a core text selected for each half term.

Cookies
Some cookies are necessary in order to make this website function correctly. These are set by default and whilst you can block or delete them by changing your browser settings, some functionality such as being able to log in to the website will not work if you do this. The necessary cookies set on this website are as follows:
Website CMS
A 'sessionid' token is required for logging in to the website and a 'crfstoken' token is used to prevent cross site request forgery. An 'alertDismissed' token is used to prevent certain alerts from re-appearing if they have been dismissed. An 'awsUploads' object is used to facilitate file uploads.
Matomo
We use Matomo cookies to improve the website performance by capturing information such as browser and device types. The data from this cookie is anonymised.
reCaptcha
Cookies are used to help distinguish between humans and bots on contact forms on this website.
